risks: Absence of documented SOPs and delegation of authority may result in inconsistent capex practices, unclear accountability and approvals being performed outside approved authority limits.
Non-standard procedures may be followed across departments or locations, resulting in weak control discipline and inconsistent treatment of capital expenditure transactions.
Inadequate assessment of asset requirements may result in incorrect capex planning, unnecessary asset procurement or failure to provide for essential business needs.
Unauthorized changes to the approved capex plan may result in projects being initiated or modified without proper business justification and management approval.
Inaccurate assumptions used for payback or IRR evaluation may lead to approval of commercially unviable capital projects.
Incorrect budget provisions may result in inadequate or excessive allocation of funds for capital expenditure projects.
Capital expenditure may be incurred without approved budget or beyond sanctioned limits, resulting in unauthorized financial commitments.
Approved capex budgets may not be accurately updated in the system, leading to incorrect budget tracking and weak monitoring of actual expenditure.
Capex projects may be created in the system without valid approval, resulting in unauthorized purchase or creation of fixed assets.
Incorrect project master data may lead to inaccurate cost accumulation, budget monitoring and capitalization of project expenditure.
Capital purchase requisitions may be raised without proper approval or business justification, resulting in unauthorized procurement initiation.
Requisitions may not be aligned with approved budget, technical requirement or project scope, leading to unsuitable or unnecessary asset procurement.
Capital purchase orders may be created or amended without proper authorization, resulting in unauthorized commitments to vendors.
Incorrect rates, quantities, tax details or technical specifications in capital purchase orders may result in excess cost, wrong procurement or financial reporting errors.
Selection of technically unsuitable or suboptimal vendors may result in quality issues, project delays, cost overruns or poor service outcomes.
Goods receipt notes may be prepared without actual receipt or acceptance of the asset, resulting in fictitious or premature recording of fixed assets.
Incomplete or inaccurate GRN preparation may result in incorrect asset records, vendor liabilities and capitalization entries.
Assets received in defective or faulty condition may be accepted without adequate inspection, resulting in operational issues and avoidable costs.
Delay in GRN creation may affect timely recording of assets, project cost tracking and vendor invoice processing.
Capital invoices may be booked without confirmation of receipt, approval or supporting documentation, resulting in unauthorized or inaccurate liability recognition.
Incorrect invoice booking may result in wrong asset cost, tax treatment, vendor balance or financial statement classification.
Payments may be processed to vendors without proper authorization, invoice validation or confirmation of asset receipt.
Payments made without adequate three-way matching may result in duplicate payments, excess payments or payments for assets not received.
Fixed assets may be capitalized without actual receipt, acceptance or readiness for use, resulting in premature or inaccurate capitalization.
Assets that have been put to use may not be capitalized on a timely basis, resulting in understatement of fixed assets and incorrect depreciation charge.
Revenue expenditure such as repairs and maintenance may be incorrectly capitalized, resulting in overstatement of assets and understatement of expenses.
Incidental costs directly attributable to asset acquisition or construction may not be capitalized appropriately, resulting in inaccurate asset cost.
Project costs may not be correctly accumulated or settled from CWIP to fixed assets, resulting in inaccurate capitalization and project accounting.
CWIP balances may not be periodically reviewed for completion status, resulting in delayed capitalization and incorrect depreciation recognition.
Borrowing costs may be incorrectly included or excluded from project cost, resulting in non-compliance with applicable accounting standards.
Fixed asset master records may be created or modified inaccurately or without authorization, resulting in unreliable fixed asset register data.
Asset numbers may not be allotted or recorded for all assets, reducing traceability between physical assets and accounting records.
Incorrect GL account, asset class, depreciation key or useful life may be assigned, resulting in incorrect classification and accounting of fixed assets.
Fixed asset register may not be updated completely and accurately for additions, transfers, disposals or changes in asset details.
Physical assets may not be tagged with asset numbers or barcodes, resulting in weak traceability and difficulty in physical verification.
Mismatch between tagged physical assets and fixed asset register may result in fictitious, duplicate or unrecorded assets remaining unidentified.
Depreciation may be calculated or recorded inaccurately due to incorrect rates, useful life, asset class or capitalization date.
Incorrect amortisation of intangible assets may result in misstated asset values and non-compliance with accounting requirements.
Depreciation rates or keys may not be updated correctly in the fixed asset register, resulting in recurring financial reporting errors.
Useful lives of assets may not be reviewed periodically, resulting in depreciation that does not reflect actual usage, condition or economic benefit of assets.
Incorrect or inadequate useful life assignment may result in non-compliance with Companies Act requirements and misstatement of depreciation expense.
Physical assets may not be verified periodically, resulting in lack of assurance over existence, condition and location of assets recorded in the books.
Differences between physical assets and fixed asset register may remain unidentified, resulting in fictitious, missing or misplaced assets.
Inadequate control over physical location of assets may result in loss, unauthorized movement or misuse of company assets.
Inter-unit or inter-location movement of fixed assets may not be approved, recorded or tracked accurately, resulting in incorrect asset location records.
Unauthorized transfer or removal of assets from company premises may result in loss of assets and weak accountability.
Fixed assets may be disposed of or retired without proper approval, resulting in unauthorized removal or sale of company assets.
Assets may be disposed at inappropriate rates or without adequate valuation, resulting in financial loss to the company.
Incorrect accounting of asset disposal may result in inaccurate reversal of cost, accumulated depreciation, gain or loss on sale and invoicing.
Assets identified for disposal may not be properly tracked, leading to risk of misuse, theft or delayed accounting recognition.
Impairment indicators for fixed assets may not be identified or assessed by management, resulting in overstatement of asset carrying value.
Incorrect impairment assessment may result in non-compliance with applicable accounting standards and inaccurate financial reporting.
Fixed assets may not be adequately insured against relevant risks, resulting in potential financial loss in case of damage, theft or other insured events.
Insurance coverage may not be updated for new additions, disposals or changes in asset values, resulting in underinsurance or unnecessary premium cost.
Insurance spares may not be properly identified, classified or capitalized, resulting in incorrect accounting treatment and weak tracking of critical spares.
Critical insurance spares may not be monitored separately, resulting in operational risk if such spares are unavailable when required.
Actual benefits from approved capex projects may not be monitored against payback or IRR assumptions, resulting in weak post-implementation review.
Significant deviations in capex outcomes may not be identified and escalated, resulting in repeated investment decisions based on inaccurate assumptions.
